 Order

This petition is filed by the petitioner-accused No.4 under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the criminal proceedings in C.C.No.685/2016 arising out of Crime No.438/2015 registered by Madanayakanahally Police Station and charge sheeted for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 34 IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the D.P. Act.
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1-State and learned counsel for respondent No.2.

3. The case of the prosecution is that on the complaint of respondent No.2 filed on 14.09.2015, the Police registered the FIR where she has alleged that she got married with accused No.1 and she was living together with accused Nos.1 NC: 2024:KHC:1750 to 3.

This petitioner is said to be the sister of accused No.1 came for the post maternity care to her parental house, she used to trouble the complainant and accused Nos.1 to 3 said to be demanded dowry and also demanded to transfer the property in the name of accused No.1 as it stands in the name of the complainant.
In spite of panchayath, the accused persons continued harassment.
Subsequently, the respondent No.2 went for her post maternity care to her parents house, the accused persons came once and thereafter they did not come.
Later, when the parents of respondent No.2 approached the accused persons to take her back to their home, they were reluctant to take her back and they demanded money for the same.

There is specific allegation made against this petitioner in the complaint at paragraph No.9 and also in the further statement regarding the instigation made by this petitioner for her brother and in turn all of them were said to be harassed the complainant physically and mentally.
There is sufficient material placed on record to frame the charges against this petitioner.
Apart from that, the order sheet reveals, the Trial Court framed the charges long back i.e., on 18.08.2017 and subsequently summons were issued.

Witnesses were present NC: 2024:KHC:1750 and due to various reasons on the ground of settlement, the learned counsel for the accused obtained adjournments, thereafter for one or the other reason from last four to five years, the case is pending.

Therefore, I am of the view, if the Trial Court has already opined that there is prima facie material Smt Hemamala N vs State Of Karnataka on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190044987/
2 and framed the charges against the petitioner, this Court cannot interfere at this stage.
